The yoke lute, also called the lyre, is a chordophone of the lute subfamily, Hornbostel–Sachs 321.21 and 321.22. In construction one or more strings run parallel to the soundboard and are fixed to a yoke in the same plane as the soundboard, the yoke made of two arms and a crossbar. The soundbox may be bowl-shaped or box-shaped. Africa has a continuous tradition, and there are also traditions in ancient Greece, Scandinavia, Finland / Karelia and Britain; ancient Greece mostly strummed, Africa mostly plucks, and a few are bowed.
軛型魯特琴在不同文化中演變出多種形式，在霍恩博斯特爾-薩克斯分類體系中被細分為多: The yoke lute has evolved into many forms in different cultures, and it is divided into several types in the Hornbostel–Sachs system. Today it is still alive in many traditional music cultures and contributes to the richness of the world's folk musics.
軛型魯特琴的材質依共鳴箱形制而異。碗狀者共鳴器常以龜殼製成，音板則為皮革；箱狀者: The material of the yoke lute depends on the form of the soundbox. Bowl-shaped resonators are often made of tortoise shell with a leather soundboard; box-shaped bodies have both the body and the soundboard of wood. The sources do not state the materials of the yoke, the arms, the crossbar, the strings and the fittings, so no inference is drawn.
軛型魯特琴起源於古代中東和北非地區，最早的實物證據可追溯至約西元前1500年的埃: The yoke lute originated in the ancient Middle East and North Africa, the earliest physical evidence going back to Egypt around 1500 BCE. Such instruments have a distinctive yoke-shaped neck design: the neck and the soundbox form a yoke, with the strings stretched between them.
軛型魯特琴音色清澈明亮，具有水晶般的透明感和柔和的音質。其音域寬廣，從低音的渾厚: The yoke lute's timbre is clear and bright, with a crystalline transparency and a soft quality. Its range is wide, from a full, warm bass to a light, nimble treble, with many layers. The strings' vibration carries into the body, and the tone has the clarity of the piano and the warmth of the guitar, yet more translucent than either. Against the heaviness of the harp its sound is finer and more delicate; against the metallophone it has a softer charm rather than a metallic bite. The notes decay fairly quickly, as on a plucked instrument, and each note stands clear on its own. The sound carries well: even outdoors the tone keeps its completeness and its expression, and it suits polyphonic music.
